lines.text: This is LucentDock, a smart dock for Windows, built and verified in public.
A normal taskbar remembers what you pinned. It misses what needs you now: the next meeting, a dying battery, or a limit you chose.
Important context stays scattered across calendars, menus, notifications, and windows you must hunt down.
Ten minutes before design review, the everyday dock still carries media, weather, screen time, and the usual apps.
Then it rearranges itself. The calendar moves forward, leisure widgets step away, and the bar settles without covering your work.
The change is an overlay, never a rewrite. Activity explains the rule and its reason, while one action restores the everyday dock.
Six ideas cover the product: apps to arrange, fourteen useful widgets, and nine automations that respond to your day.
Three styles join safety that fails visible and privacy by default: no account, no telemetry, and fixture data in public previews.
Choose glass, dark, or liquid glass, where your own wallpaper bends at the rim through a lens instead of a generic blur.
Six hundred eighty two automated tests and reproducible build verification make each release artifact comparable byte for byte.
Attended owner gates at five display scales, independent audits, and explicit signoff come before installation.
Leonel Cortés coordinates the artificial intelligence systems. One implements, another audits blind, findings return to the builder, and only Leonel runs the final gate.
The first release is being prepared. Until then, build from source, inspect the evidence, verify the artifact hash, and remember that every dock change can be undone.
